alerts.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 18 at 6:37PM PST until November 18 at 9:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southeastern San Mateo County...
Southwestern Santa Clara County...
Santa Cruz County...

* WHEN...Until 900 PM PST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Ponding of water in urban or other areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 637 PM PST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. This  will
cause urban and small stream flooding. Between 2 and 5.5 inches
of rain have fallen.
- Heavy rain has moved out of Santa Cruz with flooding to recede
over the next few hours.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Palo Alto, Santa Cruz, Watsonville, Saratoga, Los Gatos,
Corralitos, Scotts Valley, Capitola, Live Oak, Woodside, Felton,
Ben Lomond, Boulder Creek, Soquel, Twin Lakes and Aptos.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
alerts.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

alerts.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 18 at 4:56PM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at
favored break points.

* WHERE...All Pacific Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.
alerts.instruction:
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.
